citations.title: Home Health Services
citations.requirement: Governing statute for home health agencies (HHAs) and nurse registries. Covers licensure, staffing, service agreements, RN supervision and homemaker/companion registration.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care. Home health aides provide hands-on personal care. The administrator definition is at s. 400.462(1), personal care at (27), nurse registry at (25).

citations.title: Home health agencies to be licensed; expiration of license; exemptions; unlawful acts; penalties
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide hands-on care. The license number must appear in advertising. Advertising services not on the license is unlicensed activity. Exemptions are in subsection (6).

citations.title: Application for license; fee
citations.requirement: Requires CPA-compiled 2-year projections and proof of $250,000 per claim malpractice and liability insurance. Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation. Subsection (2) provides for the licensure survey.

citations.title: Staffing requirements; notifications; limitations on staffing services
citations.requirement: Sets administrator qualifications (subsection (1)). A director of nursing is required only for agencies providing skilled nursing (subsection (2)). No staffing ratios are set.

citations.title: Patients with Alzheimer's disease or other related disorders; staff training requirements; certain disclosures
citations.requirement: HHA staff must complete s. 430.5025 dementia training. An HHA that claims special Alzheimer's care must disclose the services that make it suitable (subsection (2)).

citations.title: Home health service agreements; treatment orders; patient assessment; plan of care; provision of services; orders not to resuscitate
citations.requirement: (1) A written agreement states the services, the rates for privately paid services and the payment sources. (3) The agency arranges RN supervisory visits to the home of a patient receiving aide services, per the patient's direction, approval and agreement to pay for the visits. (4) The patient has the right to be informed of and participate in care planning and to receive a copy of the plan on request. (7) Personnel may withhold CPR on a valid DNR order (s. 401.45).

citations.title: Assistance with self-administration of medication and with other tasks
citations.requirement: Unlicensed assistance is allowed only for medically stable patients, with routine, regularly scheduled medications, upon a documented request and the patient's written informed consent. (3) lists permitted assistance, including keeping a record of each assist. (4) lists exclusions: injectables, tube administration, mixing or calculating doses, PRN meds requiring judgment, rectal/urethral/vaginal preparations, and others. (6) lists other tasks: glucometer, antiembolism stockings, oxygen cannula (no titration), CPAP (no titration), vital signs and colostomy bags.

citations.title: Licensure of nurse registries
citations.requirement: Referred CNAs, aides, companions and homemakers are independent contractors, and the registry may not supervise them. Used only for the nurse registry alternative.

citations.title: Registration of particular service providers exempt from licensure
citations.requirement: Homemaker and companion providers must register. The registration number must appear in ads (subsection (5)). Each worker's employment history must be verified (subsection (4)). Registration costs $50 per biennium (statutory, CPI-adjusted).

citations.title: Minimum licensure requirements
citations.requirement: (3) Report application and insurance changes to AHCA within 21 calendar days. (4) Give AHCA 30 days' notice before discontinuing operation, and notify clients. Arrange record custody, or publish notice weekly for 4 consecutive weeks. (5) On or before the first day of service, give each client the complaint, abuse hotline and Medicaid fraud hotline notices. Each licensee must have a written policy for giving these notices. (6) Proof of legal right to occupy. (14) Affidavit of compliance with s. 408.051(3) with the initial and renewal application.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening of owners, administrators, financial officers and direct-care staff. Rescreen every 5 years.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Fingerprint results are shared through the Clearinghouse. Screening is renewed through it.

citations.title: Dementia-related staff training
citations.requirement: HHA, nurse registry and homemaker/companion staff: a 1-hour course within 30 days, and 2 additional hours within 7 months.

citations.title: Additional licensure requirements for home health agencies
citations.requirement: Startup, working-capital and contingency funds covering at least 3 months of projected expenses (contingency at least 1 month). A $500,000 surety bond if any controlling interest is a nonimmigrant alien (subsection (2)).

citations.title: Licensure Requirements
citations.requirement: (1) Application on AHCA Form 3110-1011 with the Addendum. (2)(a) Survey before initial licensure, then unannounced at least every 36.9 months. (4) Change of ownership: client records transfer to the new owner. (5) Satellite office in the same geographic service area, not separately licensed. (6) Satellite duties. (7) Drop-off sites. (8) Change of address, counties served, or office opening/closing: file Form 3110-1011 with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence. (9)(a) Administrator and DON or alternates are available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday-Friday. (9)(b) A staff person answers the phone and door and can reach the administrator. (9)(c) Surveyor access: the administrator or alternate is on premises within 1 hour of a surveyor's arrival, and a current patient list is produced within 2 hours. (9)(d) An agency with no skilled services must have written policies on RN supervisor availability during hours of patient service. (10) Return the license on closure.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: The 5/31/2026 version, read on flrules.org, controls. The Cornell page may show the prior version. (1) Administrator meets ss. 400.462(1) and 400.476(1) and designates a written on-site alternate. (1)(b) Notify AHCA of administrator changes; level 2 screening applies. (2)(i) No DON for an agency without skilled care. (3)(b) An RN may assign personal care tasks and keeps full responsibility. (3)(c) An RN provides supervisory visits, and the agency must have the client's written consent for the RN to enter the home. (3)(d) On-site supervision as needed, based on condition severity and aide training and experience, documented in the client file. (5)(b) A CNA needs current Florida certification, or a copy of another state's current certificate. (5)(c) Before an aide serves, the file must show 40 hours of training or a passed competency test. The 2026 text allows in-person, online or hybrid delivery, but the aide must demonstrate skills in person. (5)(c)15 requires 2 hours of medication-assistance training with a label-reading check. (5)(f)-(h) Limits on agency-taught aide courses; instruction by or under an RN with 2 years' experience, one in home health. (5)(i) Competency test AHCA 3110-1007 (Sept 2025): all 14 practical tasks and 90 of 104 written questions. (5)(k) Annual in-service each calendar year and current CPR. (5)(l)-(p) Aide duties and limits. (5)(m) RN review for medically stable patients. (5)(n) Patient informed and written consent for medication help. (5)(r) HIV/AIDS course within 30 days. (12) Homemaker and companion duties.

citations.title: Acceptance of Patients or Clients
citations.requirement: (1) Accept only when services can reasonably be provided safely in the home, including communication through a same-language staff person, interpreter or translation technology, and assure all assigned visits. (2) A written agreement is signed and dated by an agency representative and the client or representative; a copy is given to the client and the original kept in the file. (3) For aide, homemaker and companion clients without a treatment order, the agreement is the service provision plan (s. 400.491(2)) and is kept for one year after termination. (4) On termination, develop a plan and refer to another provider, and give written notice of the date and reason. This does not apply to private-pay clients who default on payment. Help clients assess eligibility for government programs if private funds are depleted.

citations.title: Plan of Care
citations.requirement: (3) The patient, caregiver or guardian must be told that they may be informed of the plan, participate in developing it, and have a copy on request. The remaining subsections cover plans developed with a physician or APRN and are triggered by skilled-care orders.

(3) Transfer a copy of the record to another agency on request. (4) Retain as required by s. 400.491; records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys. (5) Required record contents (referral source, assessment, ID sheet, plan, signed and dated service notes, supervisory visit notes, termination summary). (6) Signature rules: electronic signatures must be authenticated and dated, with safeguards against unauthorized access and a reconstruction process.

citations.title: Registration Requirements for Homemaker and Companion Services Providers
citations.requirement: (1) Register before providing services; licensed HHAs and nurse registries are exempt. (2) Renewal or change-of-ownership application at least 60 days before expiration. (3) AHCA Form 3110-1003, filed biennially. (6) The service area is the counties within the health service planning district of the address of record. (7) Diligent effort means two documented attempts to verify employment or contractual history. (8) A confidential client record is required, listing the contents named in the rule. (9) Accept only if services can be provided adequately and safely; supply capable staff for all visits.

citations.title: Emergency Management Plans
citations.requirement: (1) A written CEMP in the format of AHCA Form 3110-1022 (rev. 3/2013) per s. 400.492. (2) Forward electronically to the DOH-designated contact for approval. (3) Annual review. (4) Report changes in emergency-coordinator phone numbers to the county emergency management office and county health department. (6) Brief designated staff; keep a telephone contingency plan. (8) On admission, inform patients about the special needs registry (s. 252.355) and document in the file whether the patient will evacuate or stay home. (9) On imminent threat, contact patients needing ongoing services. (10) Procedures for patients who stay at home. (11) Notify patients if the agency ceases operation. (13)-(17) Special needs registry data, a prioritized patient list, and in-home medication and supply lists.

citations.title: Scope of Services
citations.requirement: (4) The license application must state explicitly which services are provided directly by employees and which by contract. The agency must provide at least one service directly to patients. (5) An agency contracting directly with an assisted living facility (ALF) or adult family care home resident coordinates with the facility and retains responsibility for its own services. (6) An agency in space within an ALF must notify AHCA in writing.

citations.title: Advance Directives
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the Ch. 59A-8 rule list (eff. 7/11/2013). Rule text was not retrieved; pull it before writing this policy.

citations.title: Geographic Service Area
citations.requirement: Rule number and title confirmed from the rule list (eff. 7/8/2026). Rule text was not retrieved; pull the text for the service-area policy.

citations.title: Excellence in Home Health
citations.requirement: New rule listed with effective date 10/12/2026. Text was not retrieved; review it before publishing the manual.

citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults; mandatory reports of death
citations.requirement: Any person who knows or has reasonable cause to suspect that a vulnerable adult has been or is being abused, neglected or exploited must immediately report to the central abuse hotline. Subsection (2) covers reports of death. Seen in search results and the 2026 section header only; open the full text to confirm before finalizing.

citations.title: Clinical records
citations.requirement: Skilled-care clinical records, and a service provision plan for non-skilled clients, with a stated retention period after termination. Secondary sources show 6 years for skilled records and 3 years for non-skilled plans, but older versions said 1 year, and Rule 59A-8.020(3) says 1 year. Confirm current subsection text before finalizing.

citations.title: Right of inspection; violations; fines
citations.requirement: AHCA inspection authority and class-based fines. Section title confirmed from the 2025 Part III index; fine amounts were not verified.

citations.title: Screening of home health agency personnel; nurse registry personnel and contractors; and companions and homemakers
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Part III index. Text was not retrieved; use with ss. 408.809 and 435.12 and confirm.

citations.title: Florida minimum wage and preemption
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00 per hour from 9/30/2026. Local governments may not set a higher private-sector minimum.

citations.title: Third party employment
citations.requirement: A third-party employer (agency) may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies.

citations.title: Electronic visit verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services (from 1/1/2020) and home health care services (from 1/1/2023).

citations.title: Workers' compensation definitions
citations.requirement: Workers' compensation coverage is mandatory for a non-construction employer with four or more employees.

citations.cite: iBudget Waiver Coverage and Limitations Handbook (July 2017)
citations.title: APD iBudget Personal Supports
citations.requirement: Personal Supports staff are 18+ with a high school diploma or GED and one year of verifiable experience (or 30 college semester hours). Providers keep training records for 5 years and complete the handbook's required training.

citations.title: State responsibilities (screening and enrollment of managed care network providers)
citations.requirement: Network providers serving SMMC plans must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid.

citations.title: Provider reimbursement schedules and billing codes
citations.requirement: Medicaid fee schedules, including the 2026 Personal Care Services Fee Schedule. State-plan personal care covers recipients under 21 only (Rule 59G-4.215). SMMC LTC rates are negotiated with each plan.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator and Alternate Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The administrator must meet s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1): a Florida-licensed physician, PA or RN, or at least 1 year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health or a licensed facility.

Designate a written on-site alternate administrator who meets the same criteria, in a direct-employee, management-company or employee-leasing relationship. The alternate is readily available on premises or by telecommunications during business hours and holds full authority when the administrator is absent. Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(a)2.

One person may be alternate administrator for up to 5 HHAs only if all have identical controlling interests and are in one service area or a contiguous county (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(a)3). Verify this in the rule text; the research summary attributed the 5-agency rule to the administrator.
No director of nursing (DON) is required for a non-skilled agency (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(i); s. 400.476(2)). Adding skilled services later triggers DON, accreditation and 24-hour on-call requirements.
Report an administrator or alternate change to AHCA using the Rule 59A-8.003(1) forms. The new person must be level 2 screened. Report other changes within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3)).
The registrant track (companion/homemaker only) names an administrator or managing employee and a financial officer on AHCA Form 3110-1003. An owner may fill both roles.

policies.title: Licensure, Registration, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: Choose the track first. Any hands-on help (bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, transfers, ambulation, medication assistance) requires an HHA license (limited to non-skilled services) or a Nurse Registry license. Companion-only or homemaker-only care requires registration under s. 400.509. Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care (s. 400.462(8), (22)).
HHA fees: $1,705 license plus $300 assessment (AHCA Form 3110-1011CL). Registration fee: $50.75 biennial (Form 3110-1003CL). Fees are nonrefundable.

HHA proof required with the application: $250,000 per claim malpractice and liability insurance; CPA-compiled 2-year projections with no month in year 1 projecting a 15%+ operating margin; funds for at least 3 months of projected expenses (contingency at least 1 month); zoning sign-off; right to occupy (s. 408.810(6)); and a $500,000 surety bond if any controlling interest is a nonimmigrant alien (s. 408.8065(2)).
Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation.

Every ad, website page and business card shows the AHCA license or registration number. Advertising services not on the license is unlicensed activity. Fines start at $100, or $500 for repeat violations.
Do not serve any client before the license or registration is issued.
Rule 59A-8.007 (Geographic Service Area, eff. 7/8/2026) should be read before finalizing service-area wording.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Ch. 59A-8 rules 59A-8.003, 59A-8.0095, 59A-8.002 and 59A-8.008 were amended in 2026, and new Rule 59A-8.0248 ('Excellence in Home Health') takes effect 10/12/2026. Review the flrules.org text and re-date the manual after each amendment.

Keep a version log, owner and approval signature. Surveyors will ask for the policies and procedures governing RN supervisor availability, hotline notice delivery, medication assistance and emergency management.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(e) makes a quarterly documented review of a sample of active and closed records a DON duty for skilled agencies. A non-skilled agency has no DON, so assign this to the RN supervisor or administrator as a voluntary standard.

Review topics from the rule: clients accepted are within agency capability; assignments are consistent with the plan; services are documented, dated and signed; policies are followed; confidentiality is maintained; and findings are used to improve services.
Add review of supervisory visit timeliness, missed visits, complaints and hotline reports.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill only for visits actually delivered (verified by EVV and signed service notes). Payers audit by plan and by AHCA.
Give each client the Medicaid fraud hotline notice and a written description of Medicaid fraud on or before the first day of service (s. 408.810(5)(a)3).
Medicaid LTC network providers must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid before contracting with SMMC plans.
Disclose any Medicare/Medicaid/CLIA exclusion or termination history on the application (s. 408.810(2)).

A controlling interest must notify AHCA within 10 days after a bankruptcy, foreclosure or eviction court action begins, and may not withhold evidence of financial instability (s. 408.810(9)). Failure is a second-degree misdemeanor.

policies.title: Hours of Operation, Licensure Surveys and Surveyor Access
state_specifics: The administrator and RN supervisor (or their alternates) must be available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday-Friday, excluding legal and religious holidays (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(a)). The rule names the DON where one exists; for non-skilled agencies name the administrator or alternate and confirm with AHCA how the RN role is applied.
If neither is on premises, a staff person (clerical is acceptable) must answer the phone and door and be able to contact them (9)(b).

If a surveyor arrives unannounced: the administrator, alternate or person authorized to give record access is on premises within 1 hour, and a list of current patients is provided within 2 hours if requested (9)(c). Failure to be available is grounds for denial or revocation (9)(e).
AHCA surveys before initial licensure and then unannounced at least every 36.9 months. Follow-up surveys may occur at any time (Rule 59A-8.003(2)).
Post the business hours listed on the application; being closed during those hours can lead to a fine or denial.

policies.title: Satellite Offices, Drop-off Sites, Service-Area Changes and Change of Ownership
state_specifics: A satellite office must be in the same geographic service area, share administration and supervision with the main office, and is not separately licensed. The main-office administrator is responsible for it and must visit periodically. An office outside the service area needs its own license (Rule 59A-8.003(5)-(6)).
A drop-off site is a work station only: no prospective-client contact, no billing, no records housing, and the agency name may not appear at the location or in advertising (59A-8.003(7)).

A change of address, counties served, or an office opening or closing requires Form 3110-1011 or 3110-1011OL. An address change also requires zoning evidence and proof of the legal right to occupy (59A-8.003(8)).
Change of ownership: file the application and transfer all client records to the new owner (59A-8.003(4)(a)). Failure to apply is fined under ss. 400.474 and 408.813.

Registrants: renewal or change of ownership application is due at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-8.025(2)). Counties must be in the health planning district of the address of record (59A-8.025(6)).

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Services Provider Registration (Registrant Track)
state_specifics: Register with AHCA before providing homemaker or companion services to elderly or disabled adults. File Form 3110-1003 with the Addendum (Form 3110-1024) and the fee. Registration is valid no more than 2 years (Rule 59A-8.025(1)-(5)).
Licensed HHAs and nurse registries are exempt from separate registration for these services.
Answer an omission notice within 21 days or the application is withdrawn.

Level 2 screening of owners, controlling interests, the administrator or managing employee and the financial officer is attested on the application. Verify every worker's employment history, with two documented attempts as diligent effort (s. 400.509(4); Rule 59A-8.025(7)).
Put the registration number in every ad (s. 400.509(5)).
If a client needs hands-on help, the registrant must refer to a licensed HHA or nurse registry. Do not provide it.

policies.title: Discontinuance of Operation and Records Custody
state_specifics: Notify AHCA at least 30 days before discontinuing operation and notify clients (s. 408.810(4)(a); Rule 59A-8.003(10)). Surrender the license immediately on discontinuance. Send the closure letter to the Laboratory and In-Home Services Unit, 2727 Mahan Drive, MS 32, Tallahassee, FL 32308.

The licensee remains responsible for retaining and distributing records for the required retention period. Forward each client's record to the client, the attending physician, or the current provider, per the client's choice. Alternatively, publish a notice at least once a week for 4 consecutive weeks in the newspaper of greatest circulation in the county, giving where records can be obtained (s. 408.810(4)(b)).
Notify clients and referral sources in advance of closure (Rule 59A-8.027(11) for emergencies).

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) (HCBS setting requirements, Medicaid waiver clients)
state_specifics: Each client has the right to be informed of and participate in care planning, and to receive a copy of the plan on request (s. 400.487(4); Rule 59A-8.0215(3)).

Rights to include: be free from abuse, neglect and exploitation; privacy and confidentiality; refuse a service; consent or decline RN supervisory visits; consent in writing to medication help; and report abuse, complaints and Medicaid fraud.
Deliver the written rights notice and the three hotline notices on or before the first day of service (s. 408.810(5)). Obtain a signed acknowledgment.
Medicaid HCBS clients also have rights under their plan or waiver (choice of provider, person-centered planning).

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
federal: 42 CFR 438.402 (SMMC plan grievance system, for plan-enrolled clients)
state_specifics: On or before the first day of service, give each client the statewide AHCA complaint number in legible form with the words 'To report a complaint regarding the services you receive, please call toll-free (phone number)' (s. 408.810(5)(a)1). Confirm the current AHCA complaint number on AHCA's site before printing; it was not verified in this research.
Keep an internal grievance log with date, response and resolution, and let clients file without retaliation.
AHCA may investigate complaints about licensure violations (Rule 59A-8.003(3); s. 408.811).
Also provide the Medicaid plan's grievance and appeal contacts for SMMC members (choice counseling 1-877-711-3662).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: No information may be disclosed from the client file without written consent of the client or guardian. All information received by employees, contractors or AHCA about a client is confidential and exempt from ch. 119 (Rule 59A-8.022(2)).
Registrants must keep a confidential client record (Rule 59A-8.025(8)).
A client who transfers to another HHA gets a copy of the record on request (Rule 59A-8.022(3)).

Store offsite or cloud client data only within the continental U.S., its territories or Canada, as attested in the license application (s. 408.810(14) affidavit; s. 408.051(3)). Confirm the specific text of s. 408.051(3).

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Aide training must cover respect for the client's privacy and property (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)8).
Financial exploitation is reportable to the central abuse hotline, 1-800-962-2873 (s. 415.1034).

Set an internal limit on gifts, cash handling, shopping receipts, loans and wills. Staff may not hold client funds, be named in client documents, or use a client's card except for itemized errands with receipts.
Do not accept bequests or powers of attorney from clients.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act, 42 U.S.C. 2000d
ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. 12181 et seq.
state_specifics: Acceptance is conditioned on being able to communicate with the client through a same-language staff person, an interpreter, or translation technology (Rule 59A-8.020(1)). This is a communication-access duty, not a basis to refuse a client because of language.
Aide training includes cultural differences in families (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)13).
Post a nondiscrimination notice with taglines for Florida's most common languages.

policies.title: Written Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Before services start, execute a written agreement that lists the services to be provided, the rates or charges for privately paid services, and the sources of payment (Medicare, Medicaid, private insurance, personal funds or a mix) (s. 400.487(1)).
Sign and date by an agency representative and the client or legal representative. Give the client a copy and file the original (Rule 59A-8.020(2)).
For aide, homemaker and companion clients without a treatment order, this agreement serves as the service provision plan (Rule 59A-8.020(3)).
Include minimum shift length, cancellation terms, the charge for RN supervisory visits (s. 400.487(3) ties visits to the client's agreement to pay), and the termination and refund terms.

policies.title: Required Notices: Complaint, Abuse and Medicaid Fraud Hotlines
state_specifics: On or before the first day of service, give each client and, if appropriate, immediate family or representative: (1) the AHCA complaint number with the words 'To report a complaint regarding the services you receive, please call toll-free (phone number)'; (2) the central abuse hotline with 'To report abuse, neglect, or exploitation, please call toll-free (phone number)'; and (3) an agency-written description of Medicaid fraud with 'To report suspected Medicaid fraud, please call toll-free (phone number)' (s. 408.810(5)(a)).

Florida Abuse Hotline: 1-800-962-2873 (DCF). Insert the AHCA complaint and Medicaid fraud numbers currently published by AHCA; these two numbers were not verified here. AHCA gives a minimum of 90 days' notice of number changes.
Notices must be clearly legible, and the licensee must have written procedures for delivering them (s. 408.810(5)(b)). Keep proof of delivery in the client record.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Do-Not-Resuscitate Orders
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 applies to Medicare/Medicaid-certified HHAs only, so it is not cited here unless the agency is certified.
state_specifics: HHA personnel may withhold or withdraw CPR when presented with a DNR order executed under s. 401.45, and are protected from criminal prosecution or civil liability for doing so (s. 400.487(7)).
Rule 59A-8.0245 governs advance directives for HHAs; pull the rule text before finalizing procedures.
Document any DNR or advance directive in the client record. Aides must still call 911 for emergencies unless a valid DNR is displayed.

policies.title: Scope of Services: Personal Care vs. Homemaker and Companion
state_specifics: Aide and CNA duties (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)): personal hygiene, ambulation, eating, dressing, shaving, physical transfers, light housekeeping and laundry, and other tasks in a written assignment from a licensed professional.

Homemaker (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)(a)): home upkeep, meals, laundry, shopping, household chores and casual cosmetic help. Companion (12)(b): companionship, escort to appointments or outings, light housekeeping, a chronological written record of services, and cosmetic help. Both may stabilize a walking client by holding an arm or hand only, and may only verbally remind a client it is time to take medicine at the client's request.

Aides and CNAs may not perform skilled tasks: sterile dressings, enemas, wound irrigation or debridement, gastric or enteral feeding, catheterizing, Schedule II-IV controlled substances, applying heat, tracheostomy care, or filling or removing meds from a pill organizer or dispenser (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p)). Medication and other tasks are in SVC-06 and SVC-07.
Skilled services (nursing, therapy) are out of scope unless the license is amended to add skilled care.
The application must state which services are provided by employees and which are contracted, and at least one service must be provided directly (Rule 59A-8.008(4)).

policies.title: Client Intake, Acceptance and Assessment
state_specifics: Accept a client only if there is a reasonable expectation that services can be provided safely in the client's place of residence, including the ability to communicate through staff, an interpreter or translation technology (Rule 59A-8.020(1)). Registrants use Rule 59A-8.025(9).
The agency must assure the client receives all assigned visits, and must supply capable employees or contractors for all visits.
Skilled agencies must assess within 48 hours (s. 400.487(1)); non-skilled agencies should perform an RN-led intake assessment before or at the start of services as a standard of practice.
If the client lives in an ALF or adult family care home, coordinate with the facility and avoid duplicating its obligated services (Rule 59A-8.008(5)).

Collect the registrant record items in Rule 59A-8.025(8): full legal name, address, phone, age, disability basis, emergency contact, next of kin or guardian, physician, diet restrictions, food allergies and activity limitations.

policies.title: Service Provision Plan / Plan of Care and Plan Updates
state_specifics: For non-skilled aide, homemaker and companion clients with no treatment order, the signed written agreement is the service provision plan (Rule 59A-8.020(3)). Add an RN-prepared task list for aide services.
A plan of care in consultation with the physician, PA or APRN is required for skilled care only (s. 400.487(2); Rule 59A-8.0215(1)).
Inform the client or guardian of the right to be informed of, participate in and receive a copy of the plan (s. 400.487(4); Rule 59A-8.0215(3)).
Review the plan at each RN supervisory visit and whenever condition changes. Record changes in the client file.

policies.title: RN Supervision, Task Assignment and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: An RN, currently licensed in Florida or holding an active multistate license, assigns personal care tasks to aides and CNAs and maintains full responsibility for them, ensuring each aide is qualified for each assignment by training and experience (Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(b)).

The agency must have an RN provide supervisory visits of unlicensed assistive personnel (s. 400.487(3); Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(c)). The agency must obtain written consent from the client, guardian or representative to send an RN into the home. Visits are made per the client's direction, approval and agreement to pay.

The RN provides on-site supervision as needed, based on the severity of the client's medical condition and the aide's training and experience. The rule sets no fixed frequency. Document each visit in the client file (59A-8.0095(3)(d)).
In an agency with no skilled care, an RN is still required for supervisory visits, even though a DON is not (59A-8.0095(3)(c); 59A-8.0095(2)(i)).

policies.title: RN Supervisor Availability During Hours of Client Service
state_specifics: A home health agency that does not provide skilled services must have written policies and procedures addressing the availability of a registered nurse supervisor during hours of patient service (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d)).
Write the procedure: how aides reach the RN by phone during all scheduled hours, the backup RN, response-time expectations, escalation to 911, and documentation of each contact.
Skilled agencies need a 24-hour on-call system; this does not apply to a non-skilled agency but the policy should state that no skilled care is provided.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Aides and CNAs may assist only medically stable clients with routine, regularly scheduled medications consistent with the label, and only on a documented request and the client's written informed consent (s. 400.488(2)). A licensed health care professional must tell the client or caregiver that an unlicensed person may assist (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(n)).
An RN must review the client to confirm medical stability, and must review and reconcile all current prescribed and over-the-counter medications (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m)).

Permitted assistance (s. 400.488(3)): bring the labeled container to the client; confirm it is for that client; orally advise name and purpose; open the container and remove the prescribed amount; place an oral dose in the hand or container; apply topical meds; return the container to storage; assist with a nebulizer; and keep a record of each assist.
Excluded (s. 400.488(4)): mixing or calculating doses, injections, tubes, parenterals, irrigations, rectal/urethral/vaginal preparations, and PRN meds needing judgment.

Training: at least 2 hours, which may be part of the 40-hour course. It must include state law and rule, procedures, common meds, and side-effect recognition and response, and must verify the aide can read the label. People who cannot read may not assist (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)15). Passing the competency test alone does not authorize medication assistance.

Supervision of self-administered medication by aides is limited to: obtaining the container, ensuring the medication is prescribed for the client, reminding the client it is time to take it, and observing self-administration (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)6). Aides may not administer Schedule II-IV controlled substances.
Homemakers and companions may only verbally remind clients, at the client's or responsible party's request (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)).

policies.title: Assistance with Other Tasks (Glucometer, Stockings, Oxygen, CPAP, Vitals, Colostomy Bags)
state_specifics: Unlicensed aides may assist with the following only on a documented request and written informed consent, and only after training by the RN (s. 400.488(2), (6)): using a glucometer for blood-glucose checks; putting on and taking off antiembolism stockings; applying and removing an oxygen cannula (no titration of prescribed settings); a CPAP device (no titration); measuring vital signs; and colostomy bags.

Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)3 lists detailed permitted tasks (e.g., bedpan and urinal, non-invasive urinary devices, glucometer testing, simple urine tests, intake and output, vitals) and requires those tasks to be taught for the specific client by a licensed health care professional and listed in the plan.
Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p)10: aides may not provide any personal health service not included in the plan of care or service plan.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: The agency must assure the client receives all assigned visits and must supply employees or contractors capable of delivering all agreed visits (Rule 59A-8.020(1); Rule 59A-8.025(9)).
Write the missed-visit procedure: notify the client, send a backup aide, document the reason and notify the RN supervisor for high-risk clients.
Identify clients who depend on daily care (e.g., toileting, medication help) and plan coverage for staff absence and for emergencies or disasters (Rule 59A-8.027(9)-(10)).

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
federal: 29 CFR 785.38 (travel time; confirm against DOL direct-care guidance)
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services (since 1/1/2020) and home health care services (since 1/1/2023). Confirm the specific EVV system each SMMC LTC plan and APD requires. Florida EVV vendor and aggregator details were not verified in this research.
Capture the six federal data elements (service type, recipient, date, location, provider, start and end time).

Keep EVV data matching payroll and billing; Rule 59A-8.0095 and s. 400.497(5) allow AHCA to request a certified report of services by staff member (a DON duty for skilled agencies); keep the same capability, with certified reports ready within 2 hours of request (3 hours if the period exceeds one year).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Aide training includes recognition of emergencies and follow-up within the aide's scope (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)7). Aides report observed changes to the RN supervisor, who notifies the physician if needed.
Homemakers and companions report unusual incidents or changes in behavior to the case manager and supervisor (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)).
Aides and CNAs must hold current CPR certification (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)). Call 911 first for emergencies, then the RN supervisor and family or emergency contact.
Check for a valid DNR before an emergency (s. 400.487(7)).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services
state_specifics: When terminating services for a client who needs continuing care, develop a plan and refer the client to another HHA or provider before termination, and give the client written notice of the termination date, the reason and the continuing-care plan (Rule 59A-8.020(4)). This does not apply to private-pay clients who default on payment, but the agency should help clients assess eligibility for government programs when private funds are depleted.
Registrants must keep a copy of any written termination notice (Rule 59A-8.025(8)(h)).

On a client's request to transfer, send a copy of the record to the new agency (Rule 59A-8.022(3)). Complete the termination summary: first and last visit dates, reason, condition at discharge, and disposition (Rule 59A-8.022(5)(l)).

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers
state_specifics: Medicaid LTC clients are served through SMMC LTC plans (Aetna, Florida Community Care, Humana, Molina, Simply, Sunshine, United as of 9/30/2026). Plans negotiate rates with no public schedule.
State-plan personal care (S9122) covers recipients under 21 only (Rule 59G-4.215).

APD iBudget Personal Supports staff are 18+ with a high school diploma or GED and 1 year of verifiable experience (or 30 college semester hours). Providers keep training records for 5 years (iBudget Handbook).
Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) contract vendors for CCE, HCE, ADI and OAA programs, reviewing licensure, insurance, complaints and Clearinghouse results.
Follow the plan's authorization, units and EVV requirements. Do not bill clients for plan-covered services.

policies.title: Clients with Alzheimer's Disease or Related Disorders
state_specifics: An HHA that claims to provide special care for persons with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders must disclose the services that make it suitable (s. 400.4785(2)). If the agency does not claim special care, do not advertise it.

Staff must complete the dementia training in s. 430.5025: basic information at hire, a 1-hour course within 30 days for staff with client contact, and 2 additional hours within 7 months for HHA, nurse registry and companion/homemaker staff. Track completion in the personnel file.
Include wandering, behavior and elopement risk in intake and the RN task list.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Mandatory Reporting
state_specifics: Any person who knows or has reasonable cause to suspect that a vulnerable adult has been or is being abused, neglected or exploited must immediately report to the Florida Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873 (DCF) (s. 415.1034). This applies to every staff member. Confirm the text of s. 415.1034 before finalizing.

Report to the hotline, then notify the administrator. Do not investigate or confront; do not delay the report to seek approval. Staff must also report a suspected death caused by abuse (s. 415.1034(2)).
Post and give clients the abuse hotline notice with the exact statutory wording on or before the first day of service (s. 408.810(5)(a)2).
Screen staff by level 2 background check (s. 408.809) and disqualify for listed offenses. Train all staff at hire and annually.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Chapter 59A-8 contains no general adverse-incident report to AHCA for HHAs. Keep an internal incident log (falls, injuries, medication errors, property loss, allegations, client death) and investigate within a defined time.

External reports: abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Florida Abuse Hotline (s. 415.1034); changes in required application information to AHCA within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3)); and payer or plan notifications required by contract.
Feed incident data into the quality review (GOV-04).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Aide training must include basic infection control (hand hygiene, PPE, bag technique, equipment disinfection) (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)4).

The DON, administrator or alternate sets biomedical waste policies for agencies providing nursing and physical therapy. A non-skilled agency doing no sharps or nursing tasks should state that no biomedical waste is generated, and set a policy for clients' sharps found in the home.
Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)1 directs CDC and OSHA-consistent infection control, a DON duty in skilled agencies; adopt it voluntarily.

policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) and Client Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Prepare and maintain a written CEMP in the format of AHCA Form 3110-1022 (rev. March 2013) under s. 400.492, electronically forwarded to the DOH-designated contact for approval (Rule 59A-8.027(1)-(2)). Renewal applications need CEMP approval or proof of submission within the last 365 days (per AHCA application).

Review the plan annually and make substantive changes (59A-8.027(3)). Report changes in coordinating staff phone numbers, including after-hours numbers, to the county emergency management office and county health department, for every county on the license (59A-8.027(4)).
Brief designated staff on their duties; keep a telephone-outage contingency such as cell phones, ham radio, public announcements or driving to the home (59A-8.027(6)).
On imminent threat of emergency, contact clients needing ongoing services and confirm each client's plan during and after the emergency (59A-8.027(9)).

policies.title: Special Needs Registry, Evacuation and Shelter-in-Place Planning
state_specifics: On admission, inform clients and caregivers of the special needs registry maintained by the county emergency management office (s. 252.355) and document in the client file whether the client plans to evacuate or stay home, whether the caregiver can take responsibility for services, or whether the agency must continue services (Rule 59A-8.027(8)).

Collect registration information for special needs clients and submit to the county emergency management office as required (59A-8.027(13)). Educate registered clients that special needs shelters are a last resort and care may not equal what they receive at home (59A-8.027(14)).

Keep a current prioritized patient list (59A-8.027(15)), a client-specific list of medications, supplies and equipment in the home (59A-8.027(17)), and written procedures for clients who stay home (59A-8.027(10)). If unable to continue services to a special needs client, document the efforts made (59A-8.027(12)).

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Workers' compensation coverage is mandatory for a non-construction employer with 4 or more employees; part-time employees count (s. 440.02).
Aide training covers maintaining a clean and safe environment and safe transfer techniques with appropriate equipment (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)6, 10).
Write procedures for unsafe homes, firearms, aggressive clients or family, pets, smoking and after-hours reporting. Staff may leave an unsafe situation and call the supervisor.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Ch. 59A-8 has no specific client-transport standard. Companions may accompany clients to doctors' appointments, outings and shopping (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)(b)2).

Set an internal policy: whether staff may drive clients, valid license and insurance requirements, non-owned auto coverage, seatbelt and wheelchair-securement rules, and client written consent. Confirm coverage with your insurer; the research notes no statutory insurance minimum for registrants and $250,000 per claim liability for HHAs (s. 400.471(3)).

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications and CNA/Home Health Aide Certification Verification
state_specifics: A CNA must have current Florida certification documented before providing services. A CNA certified in another state may work as a home health aide if a copy of the current certificate is on file (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(b)).
A home health aide must have documented 40 hours of training or a passed competency test before providing services (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)).
RNs and LPNs licensed in Florida or another state, and nursing school graduates awaiting boards, may work as aides (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(q)).

The aide may be required to show added Medicare Conditions of Participation training only when working for a Medicare/Medicaid-certified HHA (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(d) in the prior version); this agency is not Medicare-certified, so 42 CFR 484 is not applied.
APD iBudget staff need 18+, high school diploma or GED, and 1 year of verifiable experience.

policies.title: Level 2 Background Screening, Rescreening and Employment History Verification
state_specifics: Level 2 fingerprint screening is required for owners, administrator, financial officer and every employee with client contact, through the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, before client contact. Rescreen every 5 years. Clearinghouse help: 850-412-4503, bgscreen@ahca.myflorida.com.
Level 2 compliance is required when the administrator or alternate changes (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b); Rule 59A-35.090).
Ownership: no person with a disqualifying offense under s. 408.809 may hold any ownership interest, directly or indirectly (s. 408.810(12)).

Registrants must verify each worker's employment or contractual history, with two documented attempts, or an attempt to find current contact information if a number is disconnected, as diligent effort (s. 400.509(4); Rule 59A-8.025(7)). Apply the same procedure to HHA hires.
Follow s. 400.512 on screening of HHA personnel and companions/homemakers; confirm text.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: Before assignment: 40 hours of training in the 16 subject areas or a passed competency test; 2 hours of medication assistance training for anyone who will assist with medication (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)).

Annual: in-service training each calendar year, and current CPR certification from an instructor or provider approved by the American Red Cross, American Heart Association, National Safety Council, or an organization accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Pre-Hospital Continuing Education, with in-person skills demonstration (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)).
HIV/AIDS one-time course within 30 days of employment (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(r); s. 381.0035).
Dementia training under s. 430.5025 (see PER-05).
Document the training in the aide's personnel file.

policies.title: Home Health Aide Training Course and Competency Test Program
state_specifics: Training must be performed by or under the general supervision of an RN with at least 2 years of nursing experience, one in home health care. It may be in person, online or hybrid but must require the aide to demonstrate skills in person (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c), (h)).

Competency test (AHCA Form 3110-1007, Sept 2025): all 14 practical tasks observed and evaluated by an RN, or an LPN under RN supervision, and 90 of 104 written questions correct. Any staff may give the written part. Retake is at the agency's discretion and may follow added training (5)(i). Passing the test does not authorize medication assistance without the 2-hour course.

An agency that teaches the aide course but is not an FDOE-approved nonpublic postsecondary career school may not charge a fee, may not issue documents called 'diploma,' 'certificate,' 'certification of completion' or 'transcript,' and may not advertise 'training for home health aides.' It may say it is hiring aides with the intention of providing training (5)(g). Documentation must state the title 'Home Health Aide Documentation' and include the agency name, license number, student information, hours per topic and trainer signature (5)(h).
If the aide trained elsewhere, the employing agency validates the aide's competency (5)(j).

policies.title: Dementia-Related Training and HIV/AIDS Education
state_specifics: Dementia: basic information at hire; a 1-hour course within 30 days for staff with client contact; and 2 additional hours within 7 months for HHA, nurse registry and companion/homemaker staff (s. 430.5025; s. 400.4785). Free online options exist through DOEA.
HIV/AIDS: one-time education course within 30 days of employment for all HHA employees (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(r), citing s. 381.0035).
Track completion dates and certificate copies.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
federal: CDC healthcare personnel TB guidance (not regulatory for non-skilled HHAs)
state_specifics: No Ch. 59A-8 rule (including Rule 59A-8.0095) was found that requires TB testing or physical exams for non-skilled HHA aides. This is an internal risk-based program. Payers, AAAs, plans, or ALF contracts may require it; check each contract.
Offer hepatitis B vaccination where exposure to blood is anticipated (OSHA 1910.1030).
Set return-to-work rules for illness and exposure.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each personnel file must contain, as applicable: aide training documentation or competency test result; current CNA certification (or other-state certificate); medication assistance training record; CPR certification; annual in-service record; HIV/AIDS and dementia training; level 2 screening result; employment history verification; and written designation if administrator or alternate (Rule 59A-8.0095).
Surveyors check files for aides who have served clients; they must be complete before the first visit.
Florida E-Verify (s. 448.095) may apply to the employer based on workforce size; this section was not verified here. Confirm with counsel.

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Travel Time Compliance
state_specifics: Florida minimum wage is $15.00 per hour from 9/30/2026 (Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24; s. 448.110). Local governments cannot set a higher private-sector minimum (s. 218.077).
A third-party employer such as an agency may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies (29 CFR 552.109).
Travel between clients during the workday is compensable time (DOL direct care travel time guidance).
Workers' compensation is mandatory at 4 or more employees (s. 440.02).
Classify aides as employees. A nurse registry is a different model in which referred workers are independent contractors and the registry may not supervise them (s. 400.506).

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Aides work only from a written assignment by a licensed health care professional and may not provide any personal health service not in the plan (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l), (p)).
Staff must report unusual incidents, behavior changes and problems to the supervisor or case manager (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)).

Set rules for gifts and money, social media and photos, dating or relationships with clients, personal use of client property, and off-duty contact. Report abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to 1-800-962-2873.

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep a service record for each client: written agreement or service provision plan, services and assignments, signed and dated service notes, RN supervisory visit notes, consents (RN visit, medication assistance), notices delivered, and the termination summary (Rule 59A-8.020; Rule 59A-8.022(5)).

Registrant client record contents: full legal name, address, phone, age, disability basis for service; emergency contact, next of kin or guardian and physician; service agreement; services with duration and frequency; diet restrictions; food allergies; activity limitations; and any written termination notice (Rule 59A-8.025(8)).

Retention: s. 400.491 controls (confirm current subsection text). Rule 59A-8.020(3) requires the written agreement for non-skilled clients to be kept one year after termination, while secondary sources report 3 years for non-skilled service provision plans and 6 years for skilled clinical records under the statute. Until confirmed, retain all client records for at least 6 years, which also satisfies HIPAA documentation retention.

Records must be retrievable during unannounced surveys (Rule 59A-8.022(4); s. 408.811). Employee and contractor files should be kept at least 1 year after separation per older rule text; confirm in current rule.

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
state_specifics: Report any change in the information in the most recent license application, and in required insurance or bonds, to AHCA within 21 calendar days (s. 408.810(3)).
Administrator, alternate administrator and DON changes: submit the Rule 59A-8.003(1) application forms; level 2 screening applies (Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b), (2)(h)).
Change of address, counties served, satellite office or drop-off site: Form 3110-1011 or 3110-1011OL (Rule 59A-8.003(8)).
Emergency coordinator phone changes: report to the county emergency management office and county health department of each county served (Rule 59A-8.027(4)).
Renewals: license biennially; registration at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-8.025(2)). The HHA renewal application reports patient count and CEMP status.
Abuse and exploitation: immediate report to the Florida Abuse Hotline (s. 415.1034).
Mail to the Laboratory and In-Home Services Unit, 2727 Mahan Drive, MS 32, Tallahassee, FL 32308 (850-412-4500, Labstaff@ahca.myflorida.com). Registrants use the Long Term Care Services Unit, MS 33.

policies.title: Electronic Records, Electronic Signatures and Data Location
state_specifics: Electronic records are allowed when appropriately authenticated and dated. Authentication includes signatures, written initials, or computer secure entry by a unique identifier of a primary author who has reviewed and approved the entry. The agency must have safeguards to prevent unauthorized access and a process to reconstruct records after a system breakdown (Rule 59A-8.022(6)(b)).
The plan of care or written order may be sent by fax and the original signature need not be on file (Rule 59A-8.022(6)(a)).

Offsite or cloud client data must be physically kept in the continental U.S., its territories or Canada. The licensee signs an affidavit at initial and renewal application attesting compliance with s. 408.051(3) (s. 408.810(14)). Note: the research checklist cited s. 408.810(14) for the data-location rule; the fetched text shows (14) is the affidavit referencing s. 408.051(3), whose text was not retrieved.
Retain records in hard copy, microfilm, computer disk or tape, retrievable during unannounced surveys (Rule 59A-8.022(4)).

policies.title: Release of Information, Records Transfer and Surveyor Access
state_specifics: No disclosure from the client file without written consent of the client or guardian (Rule 59A-8.022(2)). Keep the written release on file.

Transfer a copy of the record to another HHA at the client's request (Rule 59A-8.022(3)). On change of ownership, all client records held by the current licensee transfer to the applicant (Rule 59A-8.003(4)(a)).
Surveyors are given access to records and a list of current patients within 2 hours of request (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(c)). AHCA employees' use of client information is confidential (Rule 59A-8.022(2)).

forms.name: AHCA Form 3110-1011 Health Care Licensing Application, Home Health Agency (and 3110-1011CL checklist; 3110-1011OL online renewal/change)
forms.purpose: Initial, renewal, change of ownership, change of address/counties, addition of skilled services. File with the Health Care Licensing Application Addendum (Form 3110-1024, per Rule 59A-35.060(1)).

forms.name: AHCA Form 3110-1003 Health Care Licensing Application, Homemaker and Companion Services Provider (and 3110-1003CL checklist)
forms.purpose: Registration for companion-only or homemaker-only providers; biennial renewal at least 60 days before expiration.

forms.name: AHCA Form 3110-1007 Home Health Aide Competency Test
forms.purpose: Practical (14 tasks) and written (90 of 104) test used in lieu of the 40-hour course; request from HQAHOMEHEALTH@ahca.myflorida.com.

forms.name: AHCA Form 3110-1022 Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) format
forms.purpose: Required format for the agency's emergency management plan.

forms.name: Written Service Agreement / Service Provision Plan
forms.purpose: Services, private-pay rates, payment sources, signed and dated; copy to client.

forms.name: Required Client Notice Packet (rights, AHCA complaint number, Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873, Medicaid fraud notice) with signed acknowledgment
forms.purpose: Proof of delivery on or before first day of service under s. 408.810(5).

forms.name: Consent for RN Supervisory Visits
forms.purpose: Written consent of client or guardian to send an RN into the home; agreement to pay for visits.

forms.name: RN Supervisory Visit Report
forms.purpose: Document on-site supervision, aide performance and plan changes in the client file.

forms.name: Request and Written Informed Consent for Assistance with Self-Administration of Medication or Other Tasks
forms.purpose: Documented request and written informed consent required by s. 400.488(2).

forms.name: Medication Assistance Log
forms.purpose: Record each assist with date and time (s. 400.488(3)(f)).

forms.name: RN Medical Stability and Medication Reconciliation Review
forms.purpose: RN review before aide assistance with medications (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m)).

forms.name: Aide Task Assignment Sheet (RN written assignment)
forms.purpose: Written assignment of personal care tasks by a licensed professional.

forms.name: Homemaker/Companion Chronological Service Record
forms.purpose: Companion's written record of services (Rule 59A-8.0095(12)(b)6).

forms.name: RN Supervisor Availability Schedule and Escalation Procedure
forms.purpose: Written procedure required for agencies without skilled services (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d)).

forms.name: Client Record Face Sheet (registrant record contents)
forms.purpose: Legal name, address, phone, age, disability basis, emergency contact, next of kin or guardian, physician, diet, allergies, activity limits (Rule 59A-8.025(8)).

forms.name: Written Termination Notice and Referral Plan
forms.purpose: Date, reason and continuing-care plan (Rule 59A-8.020(4); Rule 59A-8.025(8)(h)).

forms.name: Aide Training Documentation / Competency Record (including 2-hour medication training and label-reading verification)
forms.purpose: Proof before an aide serves clients.

forms.name: Personnel File Checklist (CNA certificate, training, CPR, in-service, HIV/AIDS, dementia, level 2, employment history)
forms.purpose: Survey-ready personnel file audit.

forms.name: Employment History Verification Log (two attempts)
forms.purpose: Document diligent effort under s. 400.509(4) and Rule 59A-8.025(7).

forms.name: Special Needs Registry Notification and Client Disaster Plan Form
forms.purpose: Document evacuate or stay-home choice, caregiver responsibility and priority (Rule 59A-8.027(8)).

forms.name: Incident and Grievance Log
forms.purpose: Internal tracking of incidents, complaints and resolutions.

forms.name: Quarterly Record Review (QA) Worksheet
forms.purpose: Sample of active and closed records reviewed by RN or administrator (modeled on Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(e)).

forms.name: Closure and Records Disposition Notice
forms.purpose: 30-day notice to AHCA and clients; record custody or newspaper notice (s. 408.810(4)).
